codeReview.summary: The follow-up does add pairwise validation for direct `HMMER(...)` calls and the new regression tests cover that surface, but it does not fully close the prior scrutiny failure. `Renumbering` now explicitly opts out of the new HMMER-level guard rail and still suppresses its own pairwise check for the default H/K/L chain set, so one of the original escape hatches remains. I also found that the shared supported-chain helper still ignores the G3 fallback path, which can make the new error text misleading.

issues.description: `Renumbering` now passes `validate_pairs=False` into `HMMER`, then keeps its own validation gated behind `set(self.allowed_chains) != default_chains` at lines 133-145. That means explicit requests using the default H/K/L chain set still bypass pairwise validation entirely. One concrete example is `Renumbering(allowed_species=['alpaca'], allowed_chain=['H', 'K', 'L'], run_multiproc=False)`: the new HMMER guard rail is disabled, the Renumbering guard rail is skipped because the chain set matches the default, and unsupported `alpaca K/L` pairs are still silently dropped. The prior review for `fix-mixed-request-guard-rails` explicitly called out this escape hatch, so the original failure is only partially addressed by this follow-up.

`_get_supported_chains()` still only consults the custom HMM dir, the local builder, and legacy Numbering paths; it never checks the G3 fallback even though `get_hmm_models()` can successfully load HMMs through G3. As a result, the new `ValueError` can advertise the wrong supported-chain list for species whose real support comes from G3. The worker transcript hit exactly this during the CLI regression investigation (`rat H` was reported unsupported while it still loaded through G3), and the final code leaves the helper unchanged.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The `python-library-worker` skill still treats broader `tests/unit/airr/` and full-suite pytest runs as mandatory, but this repo's mission guidance already allows scoped alternatives and this worker hit timeouts on both commands before still reporting `followedProcedure: true`. The skill and/or handoff guidance should better encode timeout-aware scoped validation so adherence is not overstated.
